newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian cenbank says no more rate cuts for now.
newsitem.headline: Colombian cenbank says no more rate cuts for now.

text.p: The policy-making board of directors of Colombia's central bank said Friday that it had ruled out any further cut in key interest rates for now.

The board said in a terse, three-paragraph statement that its members met to review monetary policy Thursday and saw reason to be "optimistic" about meeting an annual 18 percent inflation target set at the beginning of the year.
But to meet that target, the statement added that the board had decided to "keep the basic conditions of monetary policy unchanged" and leave interest rates at their current levels for now.

Government officials reiterated calls for a further cut in interest rates to boost flagging economic growth, after reporting just last week that gross domestic product dropped for the second consecutive period in the first quarter of 1997.

But the central bank, which has cut real interest rates over the past two years from a high of 12 percent to a current level of about four percent, is clearly wary of rekindling inflation by easing policy too far. Inflation topped 21 percent in 1996.
The last drop in interest rates was announced by the central bank on May 6, when rates on benchmark 30-day treasury notes were cut by one percentage point to 22 percent.
